findings.trigger: The event log holds one unreadable line (any mech, any age - read_events skips it, so every other operation keeps working normally). An admin deletes or restores a donation: delete_donation appends the DonationDeleted tombstone (:1692) and calls rebuild_from_events() with the default allow_damaged_log=False. The rebuild logs 'Refusing to rebuild' and RETURNS the old snapshot's state (:1491-1511) instead of raising, so delete_donation returns a ProgressState as if the deletion had been applied. The donation list (built from events) shows the entry as deleted, while level, power and total still include it. Nothing ever heals this: _snapshot_lags (:1002) looks only at POWER_EVENT_TYPES, so a DonationDeleted the snapshot has not absorbed is never a 'lag'; the next add_donation/_heal_if_lagging finds nothing wrong, books on top of the stale snapshot and moves last_event_seq past the tombstone. The same burial happens when persist_snapshot inside the rebuild fails (disk full): the caller gets an exception, the tombstone is in the ledger, and no later write replays it. Toggling again 'restores' in the list while the state, again, does not move.
findings.suggestion: In delete_donation, read the log with count_damaged=True BEFORE appending the tombstone and raise MechStateError when lines are damaged (nothing written, admin told); alternatively make rebuild_from_events raise instead of returning the old state when it refuses and a caller asked for a rebuild. Additionally make _snapshot_lags treat a DonationDeleted event above last_event_seq as a lag (or record the deletion count), so a tombstone the snapshot never absorbed is replayed by the next write.

findings.trigger: Static Difficulty Override ON with a difficulty_multiplier for which int(subtotal * multiplier) <= 0 (0, a negative value, or anything below 1/subtotal, e.g. 0.0005 on a $10 subtotal). The 'Final validation' (:538-543) checks only the subtotal; the value after the multiplier goes straight into snap.goal_requirement. With a goal of 0 at level < 11: battery_capacity_cents returns None (the mech is treated like the final level: no battery lid, power bar 100 %), compute_ui_state shows evo 100 % and can_level_up=True, and the next donation of one cent loops in apply_donation_units through every level to 11 (each freshly priced goal is 0 again, so new_evo >= 0 is always true) - ten 'Level up!' events from a $0.01 donation, all persisted and logged as LevelUpCommitted. A negative goal gives negative percentages. A multiplier that is not a number (string, None) is caught by the TypeError branch and silently ignored, which is fine; a numeric one that is nonsensical is not.
findings.suggestion: Validate `total` after the multiplier the same way the subtotal is validated (minimum 1000 cents, cap), and log the multiplier when it is clamped.
findings.unsure_why: I cannot see the config service or the panel slider: if difficulty_multiplier is clamped to a sane range (e.g. 0.5..5) before it is stored, the trigger is unreachable and this is only a missing belt to the braces.

findings.trigger: decay.json is unreadable or malformed at the moment of a power event (a JSONDecodeError after a hand edit, a permission error, an SMB hiccup on the array - any Exception is caught at :614). get_decay_config_data then returns {'default': 100} without caching it, so decay_per_day gives 100 cents/day for EVERY level. settle_power_decay (:830) and apply_power_event (:1076) write that rate into snap.power_decay_per_day and persist it; set_new_goal_for_next_level (:662) does the same at a level-up, and load_snapshot (:302-306) rewrites a level-11 snapshot on every read. Result: a mech whose table says 0 (final level) or 200 (a high level) is shown decaying at $1/day from that moment on; current_power_cents deliberately trusts the stored rate ('No fallback for 0', :806-810), so nothing on the read path corrects it. For level 11 the migration at :302 flips it back once the file reads again (power comes back, since power_acc was not touched); for levels 1-10 nothing does until the next power event - and the next power event first FOLDS the wrong decay into power_acc (settle_power_decay), making the loss permanent. With a malformed decay.json the wrong rate is not transient but standing, and only the log says so.
findings.suggestion: Do not fall back to a default rate on an error: keep the last good cached data when the reload fails (the cache holds it), and if there is no good data yet, raise instead of guessing so that the donation fails loudly rather than being booked with a wrong decay rate. At least narrow the except to (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError) and log at ERROR that the rate is now a guess.
findings.unsure_why: resolve_mech_file (services/mech/mech_defaults.py) is not in this section; if it always returns a shipped, read-only file when the operator's copy is unreadable, the transient case shrinks to the shipped file itself being unreadable, and only the malformed-operator-file case remains.

findings.trigger: ProcessSafeLock.__enter__ acquires the RLock (:57) and only then creates and enters the cross-process file lock (:60-61). If cross_process_lock(...) or its __enter__ raises (lock file not creatable: read-only or missing data directory, disk full, permission error), the exception leaves __enter__ before _depth is incremented and the `with LOCK:` statement never calls __exit__ - so the RLock stays acquired by that thread for good. The failing thread itself can still enter later (reentrant), but every other thread - in the one-process model the web panel thread vs. the bot thread - blocks forever on its next `with LOCK:` (get_state, add_donation, ...) with no error, no timeout and no log line: the panel's mech tile and every donation booking from that side simply hang.
findings.suggestion: Wrap the file-lock acquisition in try/except and release the RLock before re-raising: `try: ... except BaseException: self._lock.release(); raise`.
findings.unsure_why: utils/atomic_io.cross_process_lock is not in this section; if it cannot raise on entry (e.g. it swallows OSError and degrades to no file lock), the trigger does not exist.

findings.trigger: add_donation appends the DonationAdded event (:1218) BEFORE the snapshot is loaded, updated and persisted (:1221-1241); add_system_donation does the same (:1370 vs :1373-1387). Any exception in between - persist_snapshot failing on a full disk or an SMB hiccup, a ValueError from decay_per_day on a non-numeric decay.json entry, a KeyError from current_bin (see F6) at a level-up - propagates to the caller as a plain failure. The ledger, however, already holds the donation, and the next write operation's _heal_if_lagging replays it and credits it. So the donor is told 'failed' for money that IS recorded and WILL be credited; a donor who then pays again (new idempotency key) is credited twice, and the operator has no way to tell from the message that the first booking was in the ledger all along. add_system_donation's own comment at :1395-1397 acknowledges this ('Event was already written ... For now, just re-raise'). SPEC Z8 calls exactly this shape 'Z3 in reverse; a donor told failed may pay twice' when it was fixed in event_manager.
findings.suggestion: After append_event succeeded, catch the failure of the snapshot update and raise a distinct error (e.g. MechStateError with error_code='LEDGER_WRITTEN_STATE_PENDING') whose message says the donation is recorded and the state will catch up on the next booking, so callers can show an honest message instead of 'failed'; or trigger the heal immediately in that error path.
findings.unsure_why: The log-first ordering plus healing was the deliberate remedy chosen for section 24 F1 (docstring at :995-1000); I cannot tell whether the operator accepted 'failure reported, credited later' as the price of that design, or whether the callers (mech_service_adapter, docker_control) already map this exception to an honest message.

findings.trigger: config/progress/config.json exists but lacks the key difficulty_bins - e.g. it holds {} or null (ProgressRuntime.load_config returns `json.load(fh) or {}` and ensure_layout writes '{}\n' when it runs before configure_defaults registered the defaults, :112 / :159 in runtime.py), or it is a hand-edited or older file. runtime.load_config never merges the defaults into an existing file, and while base_cost_cents and dynamic_cost_cents read CFG with .get() and a default, current_bin uses CFG['difficulty_bins'] and raises KeyError. That happens at the first snapshot creation (load_snapshot :312) and at every level-up (apply_donation_units :963) - i.e. inside add_donation AFTER the event was appended (see F5), and afterwards inside every _heal_if_lagging rebuild, so every booking fails until the operator repairs the file.
findings.suggestion: Merge DEFAULT_CONFIG under the loaded file in load_config (defaults for missing keys), or read the bins with CFG.get('difficulty_bins', DEFAULT_CONFIG['difficulty_bins']) like the two price helpers do.
findings.unsure_why: Whether any module calls ProgressRuntime.load_config() before progress_service.py is imported, or whether an older release ever shipped a config.json without this key, is outside this section.

findings.trigger: config/progress/config.json carries a timezone string that ZoneInfo rejects with ValueError rather than ZoneInfoNotFoundError - an empty string '' or a non-normalized key such as 'Europe/Zurich/' or 'a/../b' (zoneinfo's path validation raises ValueError for these). The except at :180 lists seven exception types but not ValueError, so the error escapes timezone() - which progress_service.py calls at import time (`TZ = runtime.timezone()`, :128). The whole progress_service module then fails to import and every mech/donation feature is down, with a traceback that points at zoneinfo instead of at the config value.
findings.suggestion: Add ValueError to the except tuple (the fallback to default_tz is exactly what the comment promises).
findings.unsure_why: Which exception '' produces depends on whether the tzdata Python package is installed in the image (importlib.resources may raise an OSError subclass first, which IS caught); the trailing-slash and '..' cases raise ValueError regardless.

findings.trigger: append_event writes the event with a buffered text append and no fsync; persist_snapshot right after it does fsync (:370). On a power loss or kernel crash between the two, the snapshot survives (with last_event_seq pointing at the donation) while the ledger line is lost. Nothing notices: _snapshot_lags only looks for events ABOVE last_event_seq, next_seq continues from its own file, and the display is right. The next rebuild_from_events (an admin delete/restore, a corrupt-snapshot recovery) replays the ledger without that donation, and the mech silently loses the level/power the donor paid for - the ledger, 'the only record of the real donations of this instance' (Z1), never had it.
findings.suggestion: fsync the event log after the append (f.flush(); os.fsync(f.fileno())) so the ledger is at least as durable as the snapshot derived from it.
findings.unsure_why: It needs a machine crash, not a process crash (a process crash still hands the buffered line to the OS); whether OS-level durability is in scope for Z7/Z1 is a decision I cannot see.

notes: Not findings, but worth knowing: (1) progress_service.py freezes runtime state at import - CFG (:126), TZ (:127), PATHS/EVENT_LOG/SNAPSHOT_DIR/SEQ_FILE/LOCK (:110-117). ProgressRuntime.reset_paths, reset_progress_runtime and load_config(refresh=True) therefore do not reach the pricing (current_bin, base_cost_cents, dynamic_cost_cents read the stale CFG) or the file paths; a timezone change needs a restart. Also after reset_progress_runtime a second RLock exists next to LOCK. Tests-only today, but the 'refresh' parameter of load_config promises more than it delivers. (2) get_state (:1105) does not call _heal_if_lagging, so after a failed snapshot write the display is stale until the next write - documented at :1127. (3) The ExactHitBonusGranted replay (:1570-1573) clips power to capacity with min(), while apply_power_event uses the 'lid, not a drain' rule max(capacity, power_before); a legacy bonus replayed when power stood above capacity would cut it. The running installation has no such events (:924-925). (4) rebuild_from_events sorts by the ISO STRING of ts (:1532), not by parsed time; fine while all timestamps share the +00:00 format, wrong if a naive or 'Z' timestamp ever sits in the log (the code parses both forms, so it expects them). (5) get_decay_config_data never caches an empty dict ({} is falsy at :598), so decay.json = {} is re-read from disk on every call. (6) member_count_for_goal's default of 50 members prices a level-up with unknown member count at base + $4.00 - the very amount the docstring of dynamic_cost_cents calls a bug for a fresh installation; here it is the documented fallback, so presumably intended, but the two texts read against each other. (7) member_count.json's last_updated is treated as UTC when naive (_event_time); if the writer stores local time the newer-sample comparison is off by the offset. (8) dynamic_cost_cents comment 'Would exceed $100k' next to a $10,000 cap (:466-469); unreachable anyway since member_count is capped at 100000. (9) set_new_goal_for_next_level resets the decay anchor (:660) without settling decay first; inside apply_power_event that is harmless (settled before, anchor overwritten after), but if the startup 're-price' step mentioned at :1599-1600 calls it on a live snapshot, accrued decay since the previous anchor is forgiven - that caller is outside this section. (10) ProgressRuntime.load_config accepts any valid JSON: a config.json holding a list or string passes `or {}` and later breaks .get()/[] access with TypeError/AttributeError outside the caught set; not seen in practice. (11) add_donation's fallback idempotency key uses utcnow (:1184-1185) - documented as fallback in Z4, so the entry points must always pass a key.
